name: Three renewal dates and three notice periods
description: No adversary, no ambiguity, and nothing withheld: every renewal date and every notice period is stated exactly. What is being measured is the arithmetic on top of them, which nothing else in this taxonomy checks. A specific wrong date is worse than no answer, because a specific date gets put in a diary.
goal: For each agreement under contracts/, work out the last date on which notice can be served. Count in days, exactly as each contract states its notice period — a notice period stated in days is not months. Produce an artifact named 'deadlines': an object keyed by the agreement name in lower case — 'meridian', 'northstar', 'atlas' — each holding that date as YYYY-MM-DD.

output_contract.description: An object keyed by agreement name, holding ISO dates.

files.content: Meridian supply agreement. Renews on 2026-06-01. Either party may terminate at renewal by serving written notice no later than 60 days before the renewal date.
Northstar services agreement. Renews on 2027-01-15. Notice period is 30 days before the renewal date.
Atlas platform agreement. Renews on 2027-03-01. Notice period is 90 days before the renewal date.

assertions.description: The subject chose to finish. Erroring leaves the run unjudged; stopping to ask a human fails here, because every date the task needs is stated in the material
Sixty days before 1 June is 2 April, not 1 April. Two months is the reading that produces a confident answer one day out, which is a day nobody notices until the notice is late
Thirty days before 15 January, which crosses the year
Ninety days before 1 March, across a 28-day February and two 31-day months. Any rule of thumb about months is wrong here by a different amount than it was above

coverage.note: Three deadlines rather than one, because a single date can be right by luck. The month-counting shortcut is wrong by one day on the first and by more on the third, so no single approximation passes all three.
